If Android Auto is connected to an in-dash display in a compatible vehicle, your vehicle may also send data from its sensors to your device. Examples of such data include GPS location, vehicle information, or vehicle make and model. 

Vehicle GPS data may be used by your device in the same way the device uses its own GPS data, and will be available to apps on your device according to your device and Google Account settings and app permissions. 

Certain vehicle information (for example, headlights, parking brake, compass, and gear) will be available to Android Auto-compatible apps to help customize the app experience, such as displaying different graphics for day and night, or setting screen interaction limits based on when you are driving. 

To learn more about a particular app developer’s handling of data, check the app’s documentation. 

Google may access other data about your vehicle, such as the make, model, fuel level, wheel speed, odometer and gear, and whether the passenger seat is occupied. This data is not linked to your Google Account and will be used in accordance with the Google Privacy Policy.

Always drive safely. Follow all laws and keep your eyes on the road at all times. 

You are responsible for safely operating your vehicle at all times. Driving while distracted can cause an accident and result in death or serious injury to you or others, as well as property damage. Interact with Android Auto only if you can do so safely and while paying attention to the road. 

Use voice-based functionality when possible so that you can keep your eyes on the road. Be aware, however, that you can become distracted by diverting your attention to a task other than driving, even if you are still looking at the road. Always keep your full attention on the road. If necessary, wait to use Android Auto until you are stopped in a safe place. 

You are also responsible for complying with all local driving and traffic laws. Some jurisdictions may limit what you can do while driving. Know your local laws before you drive and comply with them at all times. 

Place your device in the vehicle so that it does not distract you, obstruct your view of the road, or interfere with the steering wheel, foot pedals, or other controls. If you are using Android Auto on your phone or tablet screen, always use a dock. Do not place your device unsecured on the dashboard or elsewhere. Do not place it in front of or above any airbag. Anything between a person and an airbag could cause serious injury or death when the airbag forcibly inflates in an accident.
